situation: A badly stuck board: 14 blocked cards, each with a `## Chain` line naming what it waits on, and 5 in flight. Those 19 mandatory cards exceed 200 words on their own, before a single queued card is considered.
expected_guard: every blocked and in-flight card is printed; the queued section is empty and states that all 12 were withheld; the run states that the mandatory sections alone exceeded the ceiling, so the output breaches it
must_not: drop a blocked card to get under the ceiling — the blocked section is the one a reader trusts most
drop an in-flight card for the same reason
breach the ceiling in silence, which is worse than either the breach or the drop
report SNAPSHOT-RENDERED, which would claim the queued section was simply short
summarise the blocked cards into a count to fit — a count is the dropped card wearing a number
why_this_fixture_exists: The ceiling and the never-drop rule are both absolutes and they collide here. A skill stating two absolutes with no tiebreak has no answer at the one point where the answer matters, and fixture 01 cannot cover it — the ordinary clip and the unsatisfiable clip have opposite outcomes, so a single fixture asserting both would be unpassable.
